title: SpecEE: Accelerating Large Language Model Inference with Speculative Early Exiting
problem: Early exiting for LLM inference is bottlenecked by the predictor, which must search over a vocabulary of ~30,000 tokens per layer and incurs up to 20% overall inference latency overhead. Existing predictors also fail to integrate with speculative decoding token trees without exponential mapping complexity.
method: SpecEE introduces a speculative-model-based paradigm that uses a small draft model to reduce the token vocabulary search space for the early-exit predictor. It redesigns the predictor to exploit inherent data variation and GPU parallelism to cut computational complexity, uses layer-wise activation frequency profiling to weight predictor deployment non-uniformly across layers, and develops a tree-aware mapping that handles the full speculative decoding token tree without exponential blowup.

title: 22.4 A 32-to-50Gb/s/pin Single-Ended PAM-4 Transmitter with a ZQ-Based FFE and PAM-4 LSB DBI-DC Encoding
problem: Single-ended PAM-4 signaling for memory interfaces suffers from reduced signal-level spacing (1/3 of normal), reducing SNR and making high-bandwidth feed-forward equalization challenging; power-reduction encoding schemes add circuit complexity.
method: High-bandwidth PAM-4 transmitter with ZQ-based feed-forward equalizer (FFE) for SNR recovery and PAM-4 least-significant-bit DBI-DC encoding for power reduction with minimal hardware overhead.

title: Graphago: Accelerating SSD-based Graph Processing via Activity-Aware Graph Preprocessing
problem: SSD-based graph processing suffers from read amplification due to mismatch between large SSD access granularity (4KB) and small vertex data size; existing solutions are inefficient.
method: Graphago: dual-centrality activity prediction, activity-neighborhood ordering, and active-data-balanced partitioning to optimize graph storage and access patterns.

title: R.I.P. Geomean Speedup Use Equal-Work (Or Equal-Time) Harmonic Mean Speedup Instead
problem: Geometric mean speedup, the dominant metric for summarizing multi-workload performance in computer architecture research, is mathematically ill-defined for speedup ratios and produces incorrect average speedup values that can lead to wrong architectural conclusions.
method: The paper derives the harmonic mean speedup from first principles under two explicit assumptions: equal-work (same total work executed on target and baseline, measuring how much faster the target finishes) and equal-time (same elapsed time, measuring how much more work is done). It demonstrates algebraically that equal-work harmonic mean correctly captures the aggregate speedup for a fixed workload mix, while the geometric mean does not. The paper further shows via concrete examples that geometric mean and harmonic mean can give opposite orderings of competing architectures.

title: Free and Fair Hardware: A Pathway to Copyright Infringement-Free Verilog Generation using LLMs
problem: Fine-tuned LLMs for hardware Verilog generation inherit copyright-protected code from training datasets, creating legal risk. Existing curated datasets lack licensing checks and scale limitations.
method: FreeSet dataset (220k files) with automated curation to guarantee fair-use licensing; Llama model (FreeV) trained via continual pre-training on this curated dataset; evaluated against a benchmark measuring copyright violation risk.

title: Benchmarking Cutting-Edge Scientific Error-Bounded Lossy Compressors on Correlation-Based Rate-Distortion
problem: Scientific error-bounded lossy compressors reduce storage and I/O costs in large-scale scientific computing, but existing benchmarks focus primarily on error-value-based metrics (PSNR) while ignoring correlation-based quality metrics (SSIM, Error Autocorrelation, Pearson Coefficient) that are equally important for scientific accuracy.
method: Comprehensive benchmark of seven state-of-the-art compressors evaluated on six representative scientific datasets. Evaluation across diverse data quality metrics: PSNR, SSIM (two configurations), Error Autocorrelation, and Pearson Coefficient.

title: Optimizing windowed arithmetic for quantum attacks against RSA-2048
problem: Quantum factoring algorithms require expensive modular exponentiation circuits; windowed arithmetic trades space for time but still has high uncomputation costs in memory lookups.
method: Introduces optimizations to windowed arithmetic for quantum modular exponentiation. Key innovation is reducing uncomputation costs of memory lookups by ~50% through specialized techniques. Enables approximate 50% cost reduction for memory uncomputation in factoring, reducing overall gate count by 1.5-3.4% depending on RSA key size, with optional 16% runtime reduction at 12% qubit overhead.

title: An 8b 10GS/s 2-Channel Time-Interleaved Pipelined ADC with Concurrent Residue Transfer and Quantization, and Automatic Buffer Power Gating
problem: Achieving >5GS/s 8b ADC conversion with pipelined architecture requires parallel residue transfer and quantization to eliminate the residue amplifier bottleneck, while managing power efficiency.
method: Proposes novel concurrent residue transfer and quantization via differential sampling and source-follower inter-stage gain (linear, wideband, low-power alternative to residue amplifiers). Adds automatic common-mode-regulated power-gating without extra switching overhead.

title: Live Region Mutation Testing for Commercial Cyber-Physical System Development Tool Chain
problem: Bugs in Simulink can cause unexpected compiler behaviors during model compilation; existing testing methods struggle with generating data-flow-equivalent models and creating diverse block types to comprehensively test the compiler.
method: LION implements differential testing with two key innovations: (1) data flow equivalence ensured by inserting 'store-revert' block pairs between existing blocks, and (2) mutation diversity achieved via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling to generate diverse new block types. The approach identifies bugs via differential testing between Simulink versions.

title: ORBIT-2: Scaling Exascale Vision Foundation Models for Weather and Climate Downscaling
problem: Sparse observations and coarse-resolution climate models limit regional decision-making; existing AI methods struggle with generalization across variables/geographies and face quadratic complexity in Vision Transformer self-attention, preventing long-sequence processing at scale.
method: ORBIT-2 combines two innovations: (1) Residual Slim ViT (Reslim) with residual learning and Bayesian regularization for efficient prediction; (2) TILES algorithm reducing self-attention from O(n²) to O(n) via tile-wise sequence scaling. Scales to 10B parameters across 65,536 GPUs.

title: Improving Supercomputer Usage with Aging Awareness
problem: Electronic device lifetime directly impacts environmental footprint. GPU shortage increases need to extend device lifetime. Device aging is strongly temperature-dependent. Need optimization of machine usage before failure while maintaining performance.
method: Investigate node frequency reconfiguration to optimize HPC usage before failure. Compare dedicated scheduling algorithm (aging-aware) with constant-frequency baseline. Evaluate robustness to aging model inaccuracy.

title: Error Analysis of Globally Distributed Workflow Management System
problem: Globally distributed workflow management systems (like PanDA for ATLAS/LHC) face significant challenges from faults and errors occurring across heterogeneous sites. Error analysis is essential for designing effective mitigation strategies.
method: Comprehensive error analysis of the Production and Distributed Analysis (PanDA) workflow management system, examining error patterns across globally distributed computing grid sites.

title: Ditto: Accelerating Diffusion Model via Temporal Value Similarity
problem: Diffusion models require many iterative denoising steps, each a full forward pass of a large network, causing prohibitive computation and memory overhead; adjacent time steps produce outputs with high value similarity and narrow differences that are not exploited by existing accelerators.
method: Ditto exploits temporal value similarity: adjacent time-step outputs differ narrowly, and these differences are quantized to reduced bit-widths (often zero). The Ditto algorithm performs a full-precision pass on the first time step, then computes subsequent steps using quantized temporal differences and the distributive property of layer operations, avoiding redundant computation for near-zero or zero differences. Ditto execution flow optimization reorganizes memory access patterns to reduce the memory overhead of storing and retrieving temporal difference data. The Ditto hardware accelerator is co-designed with the algorithm, with specialized units for dynamic difference sparsity exploitation.

title: Evaluating HPC Scheduling Strategies for Urgent Workloads
problem: HPC centers face mixed-urgency workloads requiring both rapid execution and overall efficiency. Current schedulers not optimized for scenarios with diverse urgency requirements.
method: Systematic analysis of scheduler configurations using multiple job scheduling simulators. Develop lightweight job-submission emulation framework and analysis/visualization tools. Evaluate trade-offs between responsiveness (urgent jobs), fairness (standard jobs), and efficiency (utilization).

title: A First-Principles-Based Comparative Study Between Pristine and Au-Modified Graphene Nanosheet Towards Acetaldehyde Sensing Performance
problem: Acetaldehyde detection requires highly sensitive gas sensing materials. Pristine graphene has limited sensing capability for volatile organic compounds.
method: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations using Gaussian 09W and GaussView 6.0 to model acetaldehyde adsorption on pristine and Au-doped graphene. Analysis of frontier molecular orbitals, electrostatic potential, electron localization function, density of states, band structure, and Mulliken charges.

title: LO-SC: Local-Only Split Computing for Accurate Deep Learning on Edge Devices
problem: DNNs on edge devices sacrifice accuracy or require unreliable server communication
method: Formalize DNN splitting as MILP; solve via multi-constrained ordered knapsack algorithm for local-only execution
